authority.claimBoundary: Repository certainties are bounded to cited implementation, automated evidence, or explicit product boundaries. They are not claims of external validity, user comprehension, prediction, diagnosis, or universal accessibility.
authority.classificationPolicy: A classification changes only in this register, with a dated history entry and cited evidence. Filtering, selecting, expanding, or exporting a rendered view never changes authoritative state.
authority.supersessionPolicy: Stable item and concept identifiers persist across revisions. A removed assertion remains traceable through supersedes or supersededBy rather than being silently rewritten.

perspectives.label: Complete map
perspectives.description: All documented concept domains and their typed relations.

perspectives.label: Reading the night
perspectives.description: The evidence, situated agency, and conclusion concepts a reader encounters.

perspectives.label: Following causality
perspectives.description: The clock, events, routes, receipts, snapshots, and reconstruction path.

perspectives.label: Checking claim limits
perspectives.description: The distinctions and visible boundaries that keep explanation from becoming diagnosis or prediction.

groups.label: Knowledge
groups.description: What the work fixes, exposes, separates, and leaves unresolved.

groups.label: Concurrency
groups.description: How six rooms share one logical night without penalizing reading or navigation.

groups.label: Situated agency
groups.description: How recognition, support, fatigue, responsibility, and carryable action remain distinct.

groups.label: Consequence
groups.description: How one local decision leaves typed, bounded effects across the house.

groups.label: Conclusion
groups.description: How a completed record becomes narrative, limit, and plain concept receipt without a score.

edgeKinds.label: Organizes
edgeKinds.description: Places a concept inside a governing domain.

edgeKinds.label: Produces
edgeKinds.description: Names a state or event consequence.

edgeKinds.label: Constrains
edgeKinds.description: Limits what another concept may do or claim.

edgeKinds.label: Supplies evidence
edgeKinds.description: Provides a record used by a later explanation.

edgeKinds.label: Explains without determining
edgeKinds.description: Makes a condition legible without treating it as destiny, truth, or excuse.

nodes.label: CHORUS
nodes.caption: Concurrent social meaning
nodes.definition: A fictional, deterministic mechanism laboratory in which six social-trust incidents continue on one logical clock and remain inspectable through bounded causal records.

nodes.label: Knowledge boundary
nodes.caption: Evidence before interpretation
nodes.definition: The work keeps what happened, what circulated, what an audience inferred, what a fictional seat protects, and what remains unresolved in separately governed records.

nodes.label: Fixed truth ledger
nodes.caption: Incident facts do not move
nodes.definition: Known fact, unresolved-at-entry boundary, and later resolution are fixed by generation and excluded from propagation coefficients and player-state mutation.

nodes.label: Record · inference · unknown
nodes.caption: Different authority, different burden
nodes.definition: Observed conduct, audience interpretation, authored interior, and unresolved questions remain distinguishable; none silently upgrades another into fact.

nodes.label: Explanatory boundary
nodes.caption: Not diagnosis or prediction
nodes.definition: The represented mechanisms explain a synthetic night. They do not infer real motive, rank trustworthiness, diagnose people, or predict real-world frequency.

nodes.label: One concurrent night
nodes.caption: Externalities remain in view
nodes.definition: Six incidents remain active together so a locally understandable action can change what another room can notice, verify, attribute, or carry.

nodes.label: Six rooms · one clock
nodes.caption: Entry does not create the room
nodes.definition: Every room exists from minute zero. Navigation changes the occupied view, while accepted actions and explicit clock movement advance modeled time.

nodes.label: Choice + scheduled pulse
nodes.caption: Only modeled events advance state
nodes.definition: Accepted choices and due autonomous pulses are the causal inputs. Reading speed, focus, room inspection, and assistive technology do not become events.

nodes.label: Append-only night state
nodes.caption: Replay checks the causal record
nodes.definition: Accepted decisions, pulse identities, and effects accumulate in one validated state that can be deterministically replayed from the seed and ordered action record.

nodes.label: Situated occupied seat
nodes.caption: Action begins inside constraints
nodes.definition: The reader acts from a fictional position with bounded knowledge, authority, relationships, responsibilities, language resources, and costs.

nodes.label: Discernment ≠ enactment
nodes.caption: Recognition is not capacity
nodes.definition: A seat can still recognize a better action while lacking enough current follow-through capacity to carry it.

nodes.label: Support + five fatigue channels
nodes.caption: Systems change what is carryable
nodes.definition: Source, evidence, institutional, relational, and distribution support can open action; attentional, affective, relational, verification, and efficacy load can narrow enactment.

nodes.label: Carryable non-amplification
nodes.caption: Exhaustion never forces spread
nodes.definition: Every beat retains an available route that does not personalize or further distribute the claim, even when fuller repair is inaccessible.

nodes.label: Typed cross-room routes
nodes.caption: Content · format · ambient
nodes.definition: A route declares whether content, artifact form, or a social condition can cross; carrier and delivery fields prevent prose from inventing transmission.

nodes.label: One event · six receipts
nodes.caption: Local choice, house-wide record
nodes.definition: Each accepted choice writes one local receipt and one bounded receipt for every other room, preserving target, semantic, reach, support, and realized carriage.

nodes.label: Completion snapshot
nodes.caption: Close state is frozen
nodes.definition: A room's fourth accepted decision freezes its at-completion metrics while the wider night and its inbound consequences continue.

nodes.label: Live afterimage
nodes.caption: Consequences continue after close
nodes.definition: Later house events may move a closed room's current state without rewriting its frozen completion snapshot.

nodes.label: All six rooms complete
nodes.caption: Twenty-four accepted choices
nodes.definition: Explicit interpretation becomes available only when every four-beat room is complete and the validated night contains twenty-four accepted decisions.

nodes.label: Naturalized summary
nodes.caption: A supported causal account
nodes.definition: Pure derivation turns supported decisions, typed routes, later resolution, and the strongest normalized afterimage into one chronological account.

nodes.label: Visible model limit
nodes.caption: Outside the story, never hidden
nodes.definition: A separate note states that fictional interiors and modeled effects do not diagnose or predict real people; it cannot become the story's moral.

nodes.label: Plain concept receipt
nodes.caption: Encountered · experienced · played
nodes.definition: Typed scene rules and explicit choice bindings yield plain meanings, limits, status, and discriminated evidence without inferring semantics from labels or tone.

edges.label: is bounded by a visible limit
produces one event with six receipts
supplies incident resolution without yielding truth to reach

method.name: CSD matrix
method.attribution: Certainties, Suppositions, and Doubts as described by Nielsen Norman Group; the technique was created by Tennyson Pinheiro, Luis Alt, and the Livework São Paulo team.

topics.label: Knowledge and claim boundary
topics.description: Whether the work preserves evidence classes and limits what may be inferred.

topics.label: Concurrent causality
topics.description: Whether the shared night and its effects remain deterministic, inspectable, and comprehensible.

topics.label: Agency under pressure
topics.description: Whether the work distinguishes judgment, capacity, support, responsibility, and safe fallback action.

topics.label: Disclosure and learning
topics.description: Whether interpretation arrives at the right time and remains understandable without becoming a score or diagnosis.

topics.label: Accessibility and visual reading
topics.description: Whether equivalent meaning survives input method, reflow, motion reduction, and nonvisual reading.

topics.label: Privacy and persistence
topics.description: Whether people understand and retain control over memory, browser slots, and portable files.

topics.label: Release and external use
topics.description: Which claims are currently verified and which require live, participant, or contextual evidence.

items.statement: We know the current model stores incident fact, circulating frame, scene disclosure, audience inference, authored interior, and unresolved questions in separately governed records.
items.basis: The architecture and generation contracts declare distinct types, while current focused tests reject fact-binding and disclosure collapse.
items.evidence: Current source contract plus executable focused coverage.
items.testOrResearch: Keep ledger cardinality, incident binding, and disclosure-separation attacks in the focused gate.
items.decisionUse: Do not simplify the data model or interface by merging these records.
items.reviewTrigger: Any truth, propagation, disclosure, motive, or conclusion schema change.

items.statement: We know truth values do not change during play and do not participate in reach, trust, blame, fatigue, ranking, or propagation coefficients.
items.basis: The fixed truth-ledger contract is enforced across generation, reduction, replay, and mutation tests.
items.evidence: Current invariant with executable negative tests.
items.testOrResearch: Continue attacking every new effect and summary path for truth-by-popularity leakage.
items.decisionUse: Reject features that let repetition, warmth, or selection rewrite incident fact.
items.reviewTrigger: Any metric, route, effect, or summary-source addition.

items.statement: We believe repeated separation of record, inference, incentive, power, and unknown will help readers resist treating plausible social meaning as established fact.
items.basis: The learning sequence, disclosure labels, and concluding receipt repeatedly preserve these distinctions, but no participant study currently establishes the outcome.
items.evidence: Design rationale and implemented prompts; user evidence not yet collected.
items.testOrResearch: Run consented think-aloud sessions with pre-play, immediate, and delayed evidence-classification tasks; look for correct boundaries without motive overreach.
items.decisionUse: Confirm before claiming that CHORUS improves epistemic judgment.
items.reviewTrigger: A participant study or material disclosure rewrite.

history.basis: Plausible from the implemented learning sequence; unverified with participants.

items.statement: Does access to a fictional seat's authored interior clarify motive-versus-truth, or encourage some readers to overgeneralize that access to real people?
items.basis: The ethical boundary is explicit, but this representational tradeoff has not been tested with readers.
items.evidence: Open representational-risk question.
items.testOrResearch: Compare bounded variants with and without authored interior, then probe inference about unfamiliar real people and recall of the model limit.
items.decisionUse: May change interior disclosure, facilitation guidance, or the public claim boundary.
items.reviewTrigger: Participant evidence, harm report, or interior-model change.

items.statement: We know each accepted choice produces one decision event with exactly one local and five cross-room effect receipts.
items.basis: The pure reducer enforces receipt cardinality, and focused plus multi-seed evidence checks reject missing, duplicated, or mistargeted effects.
items.evidence: Current executable invariant.
items.testOrResearch: Retain exactly-once, target-completeness, replay, and invalid-action no-op coverage.
items.decisionUse: Treat one-choice/six-receipt causality as a non-negotiable architecture boundary.
items.reviewTrigger: Any room-count, route, pulse, reducer, or event-schema change.

items.statement: We know navigation, rereading, focus movement, disclosure controls, and assistive-technology use do not advance logical time or add modeled fatigue.
items.basis: Only accepted modeled actions and explicit clock movement mutate the night; same-minute inspection is idempotent.
items.evidence: Current mutation boundary and executable idempotency checks.
items.testOrResearch: Keep input-method and repeated-inspection paths outside the state transition surface.
items.decisionUse: Reject timing or analytics features that turn reading behavior into modeled evidence or cost.
items.reviewTrigger: Any timing, analytics, navigation, or fatigue change.

items.statement: We believe one concurrent night will make social externalities and delayed cross-room consequences more legible than the same incidents presented as independent stories.
items.basis: The product thesis and state architecture preserve externalities, but no comparative comprehension evidence currently establishes the advantage.
items.evidence: Mechanism rationale and implemented causal record; comparative user evidence absent.
items.testOrResearch: Compare matched concurrent and serial presentations using causal-reconstruction tasks, confidence calibration, and interview evidence.
items.decisionUse: Confirm before describing concurrency as a superior learning form rather than an intentional design choice.
items.reviewTrigger: Comparative study or material concurrency redesign.

history.basis: Plausible design hypothesis without comparative evidence.

items.statement: How much room switching and delayed attribution can readers carry before the concurrent structure obscures the causal chain it is meant to expose?
items.basis: The interface limits simultaneous panels, but the comprehension ceiling has not been observed with participants.
items.evidence: Open cognitive-load question.
items.testOrResearch: Observe route reconstruction, backtracking, mistaken source attribution, and recovery across varied reading strategies without converting dwell time into a player score.
items.decisionUse: May change wayfinding, trace-on-request, room reminders, or facilitation guidance.
items.reviewTrigger: Usability evidence or navigation redesign.

history.basis: Reader capacity under concurrency is not known.

items.statement: We know the current model represents discernment and enactment separately and prevents fatigue from lowering discernment.
items.basis: Typed actor baselines, access checks, and reducer protections preserve recognition while allowing follow-through capacity to change.
items.evidence: Current semantic and executable invariant.
items.testOrResearch: Retain baseline separation, fatigue application, blocked-access, and discernment-nondecline attacks.
items.decisionUse: Do not collapse capacity pressure into ignorance, intent, or moral worth.
items.reviewTrigger: Any actor, fatigue, metric, or access-model change.

items.statement: We know every beat retains an enactment-exempt non-amplification choice, so modeled exhaustion never forces personalization or further spread.
items.basis: Generation rejects a beat without the floor, and runtime access preserves it under high fatigue.
items.evidence: Current generation and runtime invariant with extreme-load coverage.
items.testOrResearch: Continue testing every beat, generated role, choice ordering, and fatigue extreme.
items.decisionUse: Block any design that makes harmful amplification the only available progression route.
items.reviewTrigger: Any choice grammar, access, fatigue, or progression change.

items.statement: We believe leaving an ideal visible and explaining its capacity barrier can make systems pressure legible without excusing the next harmful action or shaming the reader.
items.basis: The blocked receipt names motive, pressure, missing support, enactment gap, and dominant fatigue while preserving responsibility; participant interpretation is untested.
items.evidence: Implemented causal explanation and ethical rationale; no reception evidence.
items.testOrResearch: Use cognitive interviews after blocked choices to test whether readers distinguish explanation, inevitability, responsibility, and available fallback action.
items.decisionUse: Confirm before treating the blocked-receipt pattern as cognitively or affectively successful.
items.reviewTrigger: Participant evidence or blocked-receipt copy change.

history.basis: Plausible from the causal receipt; affective outcome unverified.

items.statement: Which barriers do readers understand as structural support gaps, and which do they misread as fixed personality or permission to disengage?
items.basis: The model makes the distinction explicit, but different readers may still import individualizing explanations.
items.evidence: Open interpretation and harm question.
items.testOrResearch: Probe explanation, responsibility allocation, and proposed next actions across several blocked-receipt variants and audience contexts.
items.decisionUse: May change barrier language, support visualization, model limits, or facilitation notes.
items.reviewTrigger: Participant evidence, misuse report, or fatigue-model revision.

items.statement: We know analytic classifications remain sealed until all six rooms close and the completed-night reading order is naturalized summary, visible model limit, then plain concept receipt.
items.basis: Completion gates, render order, and source inspections prohibit premature analytic surfaces and the historical tabbed receipt structure.
items.evidence: Current source-bound disclosure and reading-order contract.
items.testOrResearch: Preserve completion, accessibility-tree, DOM-order, and no-tab/no-Heart negative checks.
items.decisionUse: Do not move the concept taxonomy into active play or fragment the conclusion into competing panels.
items.reviewTrigger: Any disclosure, navigation, conclusion, or accessibility-tree change.

items.statement: We know concept status is derived from accepted-scene rules, matched effect receipts, and explicit choice bindings rather than from labels, intent, tags, prose, or tone.
items.basis: The pure concept-receipt builder retains independent scene, effect, and decision provenance and is attacked by prose-mutation and removed-binding tests.
items.evidence: Current typed derivation with adversarial executable tests.
items.testOrResearch: Keep independent provenance and semantic-mutation attacks whenever concepts or copy change.
items.decisionUse: Reject any shortcut that reads user-facing language as the semantic authority.
items.reviewTrigger: Any lesson, binding, effect, status, or conclusion-copy change.

items.statement: We believe a continuous naturalized account followed by a separate plain receipt will preserve experiential coherence while still making the underlying concepts inspectable.
items.basis: The two surfaces have deliberately different jobs and pass source-level copy and reading-order gates; comparative comprehension and preference evidence is absent.
items.evidence: Implemented and source-verified presentation hypothesis.
items.testOrResearch: Compare causal reconstruction, concept explanation, model-limit recall, and reading continuity against bounded alternate conclusion structures.
items.decisionUse: Confirm before claiming the current conclusion improves understanding or engagement.
items.reviewTrigger: Participant evidence or material conclusion rewrite.

history.basis: Coherent design rationale; user outcome unverified.

items.statement: After time has passed, which causal relationships and claim limits do readers retain, and which parts of the night collapse into a simpler moral?
items.basis: Current checks establish derivation and presentation, not delayed comprehension or resistance to narrative compression.
items.evidence: Open delayed-learning question.
items.testOrResearch: Use immediate and delayed reconstruction interviews, asking for evidence, unknowns, causal routes, and prohibited generalizations rather than a satisfaction score alone.
items.decisionUse: May change the receipt, revisit tools, facilitation material, or public learning claims.
items.reviewTrigger: Delayed study evidence or a new learning claim.

items.statement: We know current automated checks cover semantic landmarks, keyboard contracts, visible focus, disclosure parity, reduced motion, forced colors, reflow rules, and non-color status labels, but do not establish full accessibility conformance.
items.basis: The accessibility specification distinguishes source evidence from manual browser and assistive-technology evidence, and release status keeps those gates open.
items.evidence: Current automated contract with an explicit evidence ceiling.
items.testOrResearch: Continue automated regression checks and complete the named manual matrix on the exact release binding.
items.decisionUse: Do not convert passing static checks into an unqualified accessibility claim.
items.reviewTrigger: Any interaction, style, disclosure, build, or release-binding change.

history.basis: Certainty is the bounded state of evidence, not a conformance claim.

items.statement: We know the documented interaction model requires equivalent text for graphs and makes reading pace, input method, focus, zoom, and assistive technology irrelevant to modeled outcomes.
items.basis: Accessibility and mutation contracts require semantic alternatives and exclude interface inspection from night-state transitions.
items.evidence: Current design and source-bound invariant.
items.testOrResearch: Preserve canonical text equivalents and state-idempotency checks for every new visual or interactive documentation surface.
items.decisionUse: Treat visual exploration as supplementary and never as the only source of meaning.
items.reviewTrigger: Any graph, timing, input, or documentation interaction change.

items.statement: We believe searchable, keyboard-operable maps with complete static text equivalents will let different readers inspect complexity without making the visual graph a comprehension prerequisite.
items.basis: The exported documentation uses progressive enhancement and a canonical text list, but it has not yet been exercised with assistive-technology users.
items.evidence: Standards-informed implementation hypothesis; usability evidence pending.
items.testOrResearch: Run keyboard, VoiceOver, NVDA, zoom, reflow, forced-colors, and reduced-motion tasks on both no-script and enhanced editions with representative readers.
items.decisionUse: Confirm before calling the interactive maps easier or more accessible than the Markdown source alone.
items.reviewTrigger: Manual map review or interaction redesign.

history.basis: Progressive enhancement is implemented; reader outcome unverified.

items.statement: Where do current CHORUS and documentation interactions fail under VoiceOver, NVDA, touch, 400% reflow, forced colors, or a second browser engine?
items.basis: Those current-source manual observations remain open in the release record.
items.evidence: Explicitly unverified release boundary.
items.testOrResearch: Execute the manual assistive-technology and viewport matrix against one exact source digest and retain failures, corrections, and reruns.
items.decisionUse: Blocks unqualified accessibility and release-completion claims; defects may change interaction or styling.
items.reviewTrigger: Completion of any named manual run or source-binding change.

items.statement: We know an open-tab, memory-only session is the default and a browser slot is written only after explicit per-slot enablement and save action.
items.basis: The save model has no import-time storage effect, and focused tests verify consent and selected-key isolation.
items.evidence: Current persistence contract with executable storage tests.
items.testOrResearch: Keep zero-import-write, per-slot consent, inventory, deletion, and corrupt-slot isolation checks.
items.decisionUse: Reject automatic persistence, inventory reads, or cross-slot writes.
items.reviewTrigger: Any storage, privacy-panel, save, or browser-platform change.

items.statement: We know portable input is bounded, previewed, integrity-checked, reconstructed through ordinary generation and reduction, and rejected before state replacement when validation fails.
items.basis: Save parsing and replay reject malformed, oversized, foreign, unsupported, or fabricated state even when a checksum is recomputed.
items.evidence: Current fail-closed import and reconstruction evidence.
items.testOrResearch: Retain hostile size, depth, type, version, corruption, fabrication, and replay-mismatch cases.
items.decisionUse: Do not load untrusted state directly or treat checksum validity as semantic validity.
items.reviewTrigger: Any schema, parser, migration, reconstruction, or export change.

items.statement: We believe separating open-tab memory, optional browser slots, and portable files in one progressively disclosed privacy destination will improve control and trust without interrupting play.
items.basis: The interface exposes distinct scope, consent, preview, and deletion language, but users' storage mental models have not been studied.
items.evidence: Implemented privacy rationale; comprehension and trust effects unknown.
items.testOrResearch: Ask readers to predict what survives close, reload, another profile, export, clear, and corrupt import before and after using the controls.
items.decisionUse: Confirm before claiming the controls communicate privacy effectively.
items.reviewTrigger: Privacy comprehension evidence or control redesign.

history.basis: Clear architecture does not establish user comprehension.

items.statement: Which storage boundary do readers misunderstand most often: open-tab loss, browser-profile scope, explicit slot consent, or player-controlled file transfer?
items.basis: The distinctions are implemented and documented, but no observed comprehension evidence identifies the remaining failure point.
items.evidence: Open privacy mental-model question.
items.testOrResearch: Use scenario-based prediction and recovery tasks, including cancel, clear, corrupt file, version mismatch, and another-profile cases.
items.decisionUse: May change labels, ordering, confirmation, recovery copy, or whether a control remains in the shared drawer.
items.reviewTrigger: Observed comprehension evidence or persistence change.

history.basis: No observed storage mental-model evidence exists.

items.statement: We know the current generator-version-14 source passed its recorded automated working-tree gate, while release promotion remains held for renewed browser, assistive-technology, route, dependency, mobile, and neutral-distribution evidence on the exact promoted binding.
items.basis: The release record separates current automated evidence from historical browser and distribution runs rather than relabeling earlier results.
items.evidence: Time- and source-bounded release status; not a permanent production-readiness claim.
items.testOrResearch: Renew every open promotion gate on one exact source digest and preserve failed observations and corrections.
items.decisionUse: Continue to describe the build as held rather than fully promoted until the evidence set closes.
items.reviewTrigger: Any source, dependency, deployment, evidence, or release-decision change.

history.basis: Certainty is the bounded release decision and its explicit open gates.

items.statement: We know CHORUS is a synthetic explanatory model and currently has no evidence that it predicts real behavior, diagnoses people, measures player judgment, or establishes real-world learning transfer.
items.basis: Those uses are prohibited by the thesis and limitations, and no external participant or predictive validation record is present.
items.evidence: Explicit product boundary and absence-of-evidence statement.
items.testOrResearch: Keep public language within the established evidence ceiling; evaluate any new claim before publication.
items.decisionUse: Reject diagnostic, predictive, personnel, trust-scoring, or universal learning claims.
items.reviewTrigger: Any study, public claim, audience expansion, or product-positioning change.

history.basis: The known fact is the current evidence boundary, not proof of no possible effect.

items.statement: We believe the PG-bounded, local-first, inspectable form may support useful reflection in household, classroom, library, civic, and professional-learning contexts without flattening the represented social systems.
items.basis: The content, privacy, accessibility, and explanation boundaries were designed for those contexts, but contextual pilots and transfer evidence do not yet establish suitability or benefit.
items.evidence: Audience and deployment hypothesis; external evidence absent.
items.testOrResearch: Run small, consented contextual pilots with facilitators and participants; examine comprehension, burden, misapplication, accessibility, and delayed transfer separately.
items.decisionUse: Confirm per context before making audience-specific benefit or adoption claims.
items.reviewTrigger: Contextual pilot, facilitator feedback, harm report, or audience change.

history.basis: Intended audience fit is plausible but unverified.

items.statement: Which audiences retain CHORUS's distinctions and transfer them responsibly without turning the work into a detector, personality theory, or interpersonal targeting frame?
items.basis: External validity, delayed transfer, facilitator effects, and misuse pathways remain unmeasured.
items.evidence: Open external-validity and misuse question.
items.testOrResearch: Use staged contextual studies with delayed follow-up, prohibited-inference probes, accessibility review, facilitator comparison, and explicit adverse-use red teaming.
items.decisionUse: May narrow audiences, add facilitation requirements, change public positioning, or stop a deployment context.
items.reviewTrigger: Any external study, deployment, misuse report, or audience claim.

history.basis: Responsible transfer has not been established.
